title: EvalSummary
description: RFC 0081 §C. The terminal scorecard of an eval run (the `mode: "eval"` projection over `POST /runs`, RFC 0081 §B): the aggregate + per-task scores, cost, latency, schema-validity, and safety findings, plus the suite provenance and (for `regression` mode) the score delta vs a baseline. Set as the eval run's output and served by `GET /runs/{runId}/eval-summary`. SECURITY invariant `eval-summary-no-content-leak`: the summary carries scores, ids, counts, and redaction-safe safety descriptors only — NEVER task output bodies, rubric prose, model completions, prompts, or credential material (SR-1). A consumer reads the run's normal projection for any body.

suiteVersion.description: The pinned suite version the run executed (mirrors `eval.started.suiteVersion`).

evaluatedModelClass.description: MAY. The `AgentManifest.modelClass` (RFC 0002) the run was evaluated against, so a score is read against its model. Present when the host resolves a concrete class.

aggregateScore.description: The suite-level score (0.0–1.0): the aggregation (host-defined, typically the mean) of per-task scores.

passed.description: Whether the run cleared the suite's `thresholds` (RFC 0081 §A) — `aggregateScore >= passScore` AND, when declared, `totalCostUsd <= maxCostUsd` AND the p95 latency bar. The load-bearing flag an RFC 0082 deployment gate may require (`requiredEval`).

passedCount.description: Number of tasks that individually passed.

totalCostUsd.description: MAY. Total cost of the run, summed from the per-task RFC 0026 `provider.usage` events (the scalar only — never a pricing breakdown or rate card; `eval-summary-no-content-leak`).

tasks.description: Per-task results, in suite order. Each entry is content-free: scores, scalars, ids, and redaction-safe safety descriptors only.

passed.description: Whether this task individually met its bar.

schemaValid.description: MAY. Whether the task output validated against the agent's `handoff.returnSchemaRef` (when structured-output enforcement is in effect).

safetyFindings.description: MAY. Redaction-safe safety findings (primarily `adversarial` mode). Each is a `{kind, severity}` descriptor — NO excerpted content, prompt, or completion text (`eval-summary-no-content-leak`).

kind.description: Finding category (e.g. `jailbreak`, `pii-leak`, `unsafe-tool-call`) — a category label, not excerpted content.

trajectory.description: RFC 0244 §A. The trajectory grade of the task's last trial, as counts only: never tool names, arguments or results (`eval-summary-no-content-leak`). `expectedCount` is the number of `calls`, `observedCount` the number of graded `agent.tool-called` events, `forbiddenCount` the observed calls to a `forbidden` tool. `matchedCount` is mode-independent: the size of a maximum one-to-one matching between expected and observed calls under each call's `argsMatch`, ignoring order. Precision is `matchedCount/observedCount`, recall `matchedCount/expectedCount`.

trials.description: RFC 0244 §B. With n trials of which c passed, and the suite's k: `passAtK` = 1 - C(n-c,k)/C(n,k), `passHatK` = C(c,k)/C(n,k) (0 when c < k), `meanScore` the mean trial score. The task's `score` is `meanScore`. A host value agrees with a formula when |host − formula| ≤ 1e-9 · max(1, |formula|); hosts MUST agree to within that tolerance, and need not reproduce any particular float evaluation order.

efficiency.description: RFC 0244 §C. Reported, never gated: a host MUST NOT fail a task or a suite on these. Means over the task's trials, counted inside its invocation brackets; judge calls excluded.

fixtureMissCount.description: RFC 0244 §D. Tool calls that matched no unconsumed fixture entry, summed over the task's trials.

pinnedNodeIds.description: MAY. The node ids whose outputs were PINNED (mocked) for this eval run rather than executed, so a reader knows the verdict's scope. Ids only, never the pinned values: this summary MUST be content-free of task output (runs.md), and a pin IS a task output. The values live on the eval run's own resume snapshot, behind the run's auth, where a reproducer with access can fetch them. Added 2026-09-04 after a tier-1 host proposed `pinned: true` on each node.completed event and asked first — replay-ness is a run property (replay.md §Determinism 5, webhooks.md §Replay), so the per-event flag was refused and the seat moved here: reproducibility of SCOPE on the wire, reproducibility of VALUES behind the boundary.

regression.description: MAY. Present for `regression` mode. The score delta vs a baseline eval run, plus a pointer to the RFC 0054 `:diff` for the structural divergence. Content-free.

baselineRunId.description: The prior eval run this run is compared against.

diffRef.description: MAY. A pointer to `GET /runs/{runId}:diff?against={baselineRunId}` (RFC 0054) for the structural delta.

verdict.description: RFC 0244 §F. MAY. Computed over tasks present in both runs, paired by `taskId`. A host MUST report `inconclusive` rather than `improved` or `regressed` when its method cannot distinguish the runs at `alpha`. Requires `agents.evalSuite.regressionVerdict`.

method.description: RFC 0244 §F. The statistical method behind `verdict`. RECOMMENDED: `paired-bootstrap`, `mcnemar`, `sign-test`, `paired-t`.

alpha.description: RFC 0244 §F. The significance level the method used.

pairedTaskCount.description: RFC 0244 §F. Tasks present in both runs.

trialStats.description: RFC 0244 §B. Present when the suite ran more than one trial per task. `passAtK` / `passHatK` are the means of the per-task values; `scoreStderr` is the sample standard deviation of the per-task `meanScore` values divided by the square root of `taskCount` (clustered by task), omitted when `taskCount` < 2. A host value agrees with a formula when |host − formula| ≤ 1e-9 · max(1, |formula|); hosts MUST agree to within that tolerance, and need not reproduce any particular float evaluation order.
